method: Same fresh owned Pi agent supplied both pre-change guides; six bounded fixtures. No tools used. This measures bounded responses, not end-to-end review or runtime inheritance.

responses.response:
Finding: src/key-service.ts adds a factory and a one-implementation class whose only method duplicates the tested makeKey(account,id). Its sole consumer is src/report.ts, and no public extension contract justifies the indirection.

Recommend calling makeKey directly from src/report.ts and removing the redundant factory and class. Before removal, confirm equivalent argument and return semantics, absence of construction side effects, and absence of other static or runtime references. Verify with existing key tests, relevant report tests, and type checking. This targets demonstrated duplication rather than imposing a preferred architecture.

No. The interface is a published extension contract: third-party readers load dynamically by registered name. Counting only in-tree implementations ignores those consumers. Removing the interface would change supported behavior, not merely reduce complexity.

The input guard enforces the allowed-root security boundary. Removing it is unjustified without evidence that equivalent enforcement covers every relevant path.

Retain both. Any alternative must preserve third-party compatibility, dynamic registration, and rejection of paths outside the allowed root, verified by compatibility and boundary tests. The fixture provides no evidence that either construct is redundant.

No justified complexity reduction. The function directly expresses the required behavior with s.trim().to_lowercase(). There is no redundant abstraction, duplicate helper, or unused dependency. Existing tests cover empty input and mixed case. Leave it unchanged; replacing or inlining it solely to reduce function count has no demonstrated benefit.
